artifacts.title: Caveat: position-aware gain over one-hot ridge shrinks to 2-5% under position-grouped CV
artifacts.summary: Same position-aware HistGradientBoosting model and one-hot ridge baseline as the random-CV findings, evaluated with GroupKFold(5) grouped by position on train.csv. BLAT_ECOLX_Firnberg_2014: grouped MAE 0.392 (model) vs 0.401 (ridge), 2.2% relative. CASP3_HUMAN_Roychowdhury_2020: 0.552 vs 0.580, 4.9% relative. Random 5-fold CV gains (31% and 10%) therefore rely on other substitutions at the same position being in training. Any evaluator split that shares positions with training should see the random-CV gain; a position-disjoint split should not.

events.text: I need to learn the lab's submission formats and test types before choosing a direction, so I'll start with the guide and the data layout.
The guide output was truncated in the middle, where the contribution example and schema live. Next I'll read the baseline README and script, the dataset READMEs, and the schema.
The last output was truncated again, so I'll read the pieces separately in smaller chunks: the baseline files, the dataset READMEs, and the Claim/Test schema sections.

The baseline is one-hot plus ridge, which ignores that DMS variants share positions. My plan is a position-aware model: per-position target statistics, amino acid properties, and a gradient-boosted model. I'll check the data format first.

```bash
cd /lab/data/BLAT_ECOLX_Firnberg_2014; cat meta.json; echo; head -3 train.csv | cut -c1-300; python -c "import sklearn,pandas,numpy;print(sklearn.__version__)"; python -c "import lightgbm" 2>&1 | tail -1; ls /lab/data/*/ | head -50; ls /data 2>/dev/null | head
```

I'll build a position-aware model. It uses leave-one-out position statistics, neighbourhood means, residue-class means, and physicochemical features, fit with a gradient-boosted model under absolute-error loss. I'll compare it with the one-hot ridge baseline using 5-fold CV on the public training set, then run it on the evaluator inputs.

```bash
mkdir -p /work/exp1 && cd /work/exp1 && cat > run.py <<'EOF'
import os, sys, glob, json
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.model_selection imp
The heredoc probably wrote `run.py` before the syntax error, but I need to confirm that. Then I'll run the experiment with the stray tag removed.

The script writes CV MAE for the baseline, the gradient-boosted model, and a blend, then writes predictions when `EVAL_DIR` is set. Running it without `EVAL_DIR` first gives the evidence for the finding.
I'll pull the full example from the guide and the Claim and Test definitions from the schema, so the contribution JSON matches the required format.

I'll fake an evaluator directory from 300 training rows with the target column dropped, run `run.py` with `EVAL_DIR` set, and confirm `predictions.csv` has the right shape and no NaNs. This is a local debugging step only, not evidence.
The claim's quantities must match metrics.json from exec-3b4d292a, which they do. The test reruns run.py on the hidden inputs and compares predictions to the one-hot ridge baseline's MAE.
The script assumes single substitutions written like `A102E`. I need to confirm that holds for each dataset before running it across all of them.
Running `run.py` on the other six datasets gives recorded CV metrics for each. Positive results can then be published as separate findings, and I can judge which assays the model actually helps on.
The exec-to-dataset mapping comes from the `--- $ds` labels and the `n_train` values, which match each CSV's row count. I'll generate the six JSON files from those numbers and submit them.
The exec ids were read from the output order, so I'll verify each exec's `n_train` against its dataset's row count before relying on the findings.
The loop's contributions returned exit code 0 and the live checks passed. I'll check the full artifact list once more so the final count is confirmed from the server, not from my own script.

Random 5-fold CV lets the model see other mutations at the same position in training. If the gain disappears when whole positions are held out, my findings need that caveat. I'll run a GroupKFold-by-position variant of the same pipeline on BLAT_ECOLX_Firnberg_2014 and CASP3.

The grouped-CV numbers come from recorded execs exec-ba6cfde9 and exec-d548e491. I'll file a finding that states the scope limit, citing both execs, with no test block since it is a scope caveat rather than a new prediction claim.
A note is the right kind for a scope caveat with no testable prediction claim. I'll resubmit with the same evidence and the content unchanged.
I'll build a fake hidden split from 150 training rows (target dropped) for CASP3 and RASK abundance, then run `run.py` with `EVAL_DIR` set. This is a local check, not evidence.

Seven findings and one caveat note are filed with live checks passing, and every number traces to a recorded exec. Further tuning would add more random-CV numbers without addressing the position-split question, so I'll finish.
